speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing episodic cough and shortness of breath; to begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and do you have a history of smoking or exposure to environmental irritants?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (post-infectious or recurrent). The 8-week history of upper respiratory symptoms followed by a month of exertional dyspnea and cough suggests a lower respiratory tract infection, possibly with complications like post-infectious bronchial hyperreactivity or incomplete resolution. I will order a Chest X-Ray to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes.
